checks.invariant: GuiBursts.human_active consolidates the two former inline GUI-active expressions (decide, needs_snapshot) with identical semantics, same operands, and same evaluation timing; _check_control (stale-lease handback) is not substituted by human_active anywhere.
checks.result: human_active (gui_bursts.py:55-57) = bool((self.desktop.lease(sid) and not self.desktop.is_stale(sid)) or self._takeover_pending(sid)). The bool() wrapper does not change truthiness in the boolean contexts that use it. self.desktop is the same DesktopControl passed at service.py:99; self._takeover_pending is the bound AgentBox._takeover_pending passed at service.py:99, so it reads the same _takeover_wanted dict under the same _busy_lock and is evaluated at call time exactly as the old inline expression was. needs_snapshot (gui_bursts.py:59-70) and decide (service.py:545) now call human_active; git diff 530b29e..3580df0 shows these are the only substitutions and they are 1:1 with the removed inline code. _check_control (service.py:173-182) still performs stale-lease handback and HumanControl raise, is still called in _run_tool GUI path (service.py:151) and _snapshot (service.py:309) under gui_lock, and was never the expression replaced, so no gate lost its handback behaviour. _snapshot (service.py:300-326) still opens a burst only after _check_control succeeds under _gui_locked, preserving the run-5 fix. covers container binding (gui_bursts.py:72-83) is the 7dbda9e F1 change, not the refactor.

GuiBursts.human_active (gui_bursts.py:57) calls the injected AgentBox._takeover_pending, which acquires AgentBox._busy_lock (non-reentrant); no current caller holds _busy_lock when calling it, but a comment documenting the lock acquisition would prevent a future regression.
